property_summary: Only the owner can withdraw all Ether from the contract, so after calling withdrawAll the contract balance is zero when the caller is the original owner.

When withdrawAll is called by the contract owner it must revert (onlyOwner modifier allows only owner and original contract reverts here because owner==msg.sender enforces owner-only and withdrawAll was observed to revert for non-owner in original), so for the original contract withdrawAll should revert iff msg.sender is not the owner (i.e., non-owner calls revert).
Only the contract owner can successfully call withdrawAll (calls by non-owners revert).
withdrawAll reverts for callers that are not the contract's owner (i.e., only the owner may successfully call withdrawAll).
withdrawAll reverts for callers that are not the contract owner (i.e., only the owner may call withdrawAll successfully).

For any caller who is the owner and for any contract balance > 0, calling withdrawAll transfers the entire contract balance to the owner (so address(c).balance becomes 0); the mutant that calls withdraw(0) breaks this because the contract balance remains nonzero for some inputs.

For any owner caller and any positive contract balance funded by an external sender, withdrawAll reduces the contract balance to 0 (reference) but the mutant that calls withdraw(0) can leave a nonzero balance.

For any owner caller and any initial contract balance X, calling withdrawAll causes the contract balance to decrease by X (become 0) in the reference; the mutant that calls withdraw(0) can leave the contract balance unchanged (nonzero) for some X and thus violates this rule.

For any owner caller and any positive contract balance funded by an external account, calling withdrawAll reduces the contract balance to 0 (reference); the mutant that calls withdraw(0) can leave a nonzero contract balance, so the property is that address(c).balance == 0 after withdrawAll when the caller is owner and contract had a positive balance.

For any owner caller and any initial positive contract balance funded by some sender, calling withdrawAll always results in the owner's balance increasing by exactly the pre-call contract balance (i.e., the owner receives the contract funds); the mutant that calls withdraw(0) breaks this because the owner does not receive those funds for some inputs.
Only the original owner can reduce the contract balance via withdraw calls (i.e., a withdraw by a non-owner cannot decrease address(c).balance).
